title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: 6. Ten-Year Financial Forensics & Balance Sheet Fortress
question: Do the audited 10-year P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, and Working Capital numbers confirm a genuine structural compounder—or mask hidden accounting or cash-conversion flaws?

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion; ten years of debt retirement, capex self-funding, and unencumbered cash accumulation is a fact.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: A ten-year audit of Garware Hi-Tech Films' consolidated financials (FY2015–FY2026 plus TTM through Sep 2026) shows one of the cleanest shifts in Indian specialty manufacturing [1]. Revenue grew 2.4x from ₹896 crore in FY2015 to ₹2,120 crore in FY2026, reaching ₹2,384 crore TTM [1]. Operating profit jumped 9.1x from ₹60 crore to ₹547 crore TTM as OPM tripled from 7% to 23% TTM [1]. Net profit compounded at ~22% over the past five years [1]. It rose from ₹18 crore in FY2015 to ₹338 crore in FY2026 and ₹426 crore TTM [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: 10-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY2017 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating profit expanded from ₹73 Cr (8% OPM) in FY2017 to ₹435 Cr (21% OPM) in FY2026 and ₹547 Cr (23% OPM) TTM, while interest fell from ₹33 Cr to ₹8–9 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: 10-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY2017 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Borrowings dropped from ₹312 Cr (FY17) to ₹0 (FY24–FY26; ₹13 Cr minimal working-capital line in Sep 2026), while investments grew from ₹29 Cr to ₹813 Cr (₹933 Cr total cash & liquid investments) [1, 2].

web_blocks.html: Forensic Quality Checks — Cash Conversion, Capital Allocation & ROE Drag: From FY2015 to FY2026, cumulative Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) totaled ₹2,009 crore (₹1,817 crore over the ten-year FY2017–FY2026 span) [1]. Pre-tax operating profit converted to cash at 83% to 117% in recent years (100% in FY2025; 83% in FY2026) [1]. Every rupee of growth capex—including the ₹125 crore PPF Line 2 and the TPU and SCF lines—came from internal cash [1, 11]. Equity Capital has stayed unchanged at ₹23 crore for over a decade with zero dilution [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: 10-Year Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY2017 – FY2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: GHFL generated positive Free Cash Flow in every single year of the past decade, totaling ₹1,246 Cr cumulatively from FY2017 to FY2026 (against ₹1,817 Cr cumulative CFO) [1].

web_blocks.caption: GRWRHITECH: 10-Year Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY2017 – FY2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor days tightened dramatically from 26 days (FY17) to 7–9 days (FY22–FY26), while inventory days rose to 149 days in FY26 due to strategic US tariff warehousing [1, 5].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Nuances: Headline ROE Drag, 149 Inventory Days & Audit Footnotes
paragraphs: 1. Cash Drag on ROE: Screener flags a 3-year average ROE of 13.1% (13.5% latest) versus 18.1% ROCE [1]. This gap reflects balance-sheet conservatism, not weak unit economics. As of September 2026, GHFL held ₹933 crore in cash and liquid funds (~28% of its ₹3,320 crore balance sheet) earning ~8–9% pre-tax yields [1, 2]. Excluding idle cash and other income, core operating ROCE exceeds 28%.

2. Inventory & Tariff Accounting: Inventory days rose from 116 days in FY2025 to 149 days in FY2026 (cash conversion cycle 89 days) [1]. Management stockpiled raw materials and held $16M+ of US buffer stock [1, 5]. Also, tariff reversal refunds (₹31 crore received in Q2 FY27, ₹11 crore kept; ~₹30 crore due in Q3) are credited against COGS rather than sales, slightly lifting near-term gross margins [2].

3. Audit Footnotes, Foreign Subsidiaries & Contingent Liabilities: GHFL holds seven straight years of unqualified audit opinions (FY20–FY26), clean CARO and IFC reports, zero related-party loans to directors/KMPs, and strong credit ratings (ICRA AA Stable / CARE AA- Stable, July 2026; total debt including lease liabilities and acceptances was ₹28.29 crore or 0.01x gearing in FY26). However, three footnote items merit ongoing monitoring: (i) the FY2025–26 consolidated audit opinion relied solely on component auditors for two foreign subsidiaries (US & UK) holding ₹215.23 crore of assets and ₹764.56 crore of revenue (~36% of consolidated FY26 sales); (ii) contingent liabilities and commitments stood at ₹215.74 crore, including an unprovided ₹18.37 crore disputed tax demand; and (iii) promoter-director remuneration agreements include minimum-payout clauses even in loss years, alongside a minor ₹25 lakh MPCB boiler-trial penalty in Q2 FY2027 [2].

web_blocks.html: Earnings Quality & Capital Efficiency Forensics: Garware's 10-year statements confirm that accounting profits match real cash generation [1]. Cumulative CFO (FY17–FY26) reached ₹1,817 Cr against cumulative PAT of ₹1,554 Cr (117% CFO/PAT conversion; 12-year FY15–FY26 CFO totaled ₹2,009 Cr) [1]. Cumulative 10-year Free Cash Flow totaled ₹1,246 Cr with zero negative FCF years [1]. Headline ROE looks modest at 13.5% [1]. That figure is held down by ₹933 Cr of low-yield treasury cash (~28% of assets) and a historical ₹764 Cr land revaluation reserve [24][25]. Stripping out surplus cash and revaluation reserves, core operating ROCE exceeds 28%–32% [24], proving elite capital efficiency.

book_paragraphs: Numbers don't lie, though they sometimes whisper. When we lay out ten years of Garware Hi-Tech Films' audited profit-and-loss, balance sheet, and cash flow statements side by side, the story they tell is remarkably consistent—with three important forensic footnotes that every serious investor needs to understand.

First, look at the income statement arc from FY2015 to TTM September 2026. Sales grew from ₹896 crore to ₹2,384 crore, a solid 2.7-times expansion. But operating profit exploded more than ninefold, from ₹60 crore to ₹547 crore, as operating margins tripled from 7% to 23%. Meanwhile, interest expense collapsed from ₹44 crore a year in FY2015 to just ₹8 crore in FY2026. That double engine—margin expansion from specialty mix plus interest elimination from deleveraging—pushed net profit from ₹18 crore in FY2015 to ₹338 crore in FY2026 and ₹426 crore trailing twelve months, with zero equity dilution. Share capital has sat at ₹23 crore for the entire decade.

Second, test those accounting profits against the cash flow statement. Over the ten years from FY2017 through FY2026, Garware generated positive Free Cash Flow in every single year—not nine out of ten, ten out of ten—for a cumulative FCF total of ₹1,246 crore (and ₹1,817 crore of cumulative operating cash flow; ₹2,009 crore across FY2015–FY2026). Pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA conversion ran at 100% in FY2025 and 83% in FY2026. That cash paid off ₹368 crore of debt, funded ₹500-plus crore of new PPF, metalizer, and TPU lines entirely from internal accruals, and still left ₹933 crore of cash and liquid investments sitting on the balance sheet by September 2026.

Now for the forensic footnotes. First, why does Screener flag a seemingly modest 13.5% Return on Equity? Because of cash drag—and a subtle historical balance-sheet artifact. Nearly ₹933 crore of the ₹2,907 crore equity base as of September 2026 is sitting in liquid mutual funds and treasury investments earning single-digit yields. If you strip out that idle cash, the core manufacturing business is earning well over 28% return on operating capital. Still, holding ₹933 crore in cash with only a ₹12-per-share dividend (an 8% payout ratio) raises a fair capital-allocation question: management says it wants that war chest for backward integration and M&A, which investors should hold them accountable to deploy productively.

The second footnote is working capital. Debtor days are exemplary—tightening from 26 days in FY2017 to just 7 to 9 days today, meaning Garware collects cash from customers almost immediately. Inventory days, however, jumped to 149 days in FY2026 as management deliberately stockpiled raw materials and parked over $16 million of finished goods inside US warehouses to buffer against tariff disruptions. Also note that US tariff reversal refunds—₹31 crore received so far, with ₹11 crore retained after sharing with customers—are being credited against Cost of Goods Sold rather than booked as revenue, which gives near-term gross margins a modest tailwind. None of this invalidates the fortress balance sheet, but it reminds us to track inventory normalization closely over the next four quarters.

The third footnote comes straight from the FY2025–26 audit report and credit agency filings. Garware boasts seven consecutive years of unqualified audit opinions, clean internal financial controls, zero related-party loans to directors or key executives, and AA/AA- credit ratings from ICRA and CARE with nil fund-based working-capital utilization. Yet three disclosures deserve active monitoring: the principal auditor relied solely on component auditors for two overseas subsidiaries (US and UK) accounting for ₹215.23 crore of assets and ₹764.56 crore—roughly 36%—of consolidated FY2026 revenue; contingent liabilities and commitments totaled ₹215.74 crore, including an unprovided ₹18.37 crore disputed tax demand; and promoter-director pay contracts include minimum-payout clauses even in loss years.

If you only glance at a stock screener, you might see 'ROE: 13.5%' on Garware Hi-Tech Films and move on, assuming it is a mediocre capital allocator. That is why you and I never stop at headline ratios—we open the balance sheet and follow the cash. Over the last ten fiscal years from FY17 through FY26, Garware generated ₹1,817 crore of operating cash flow and ₹1,246 crore of free cash flow, without a single negative free cash flow year in the entire decade.

Why, then, does headline ROE read 13.5%? Because of two balance-sheet artifacts: first, Garware sits on ₹933 crore of cash and liquid investments—nearly 28% of its entire ₹3,320 crore balance sheet—earning post-tax treasury yields rather than factory returns. Second, the fixed asset base carries a historical ₹764 crore revaluation reserve. When you strip out that idle cash and revaluation noise, the core manufacturing business is earning north of 28% to 32% ROCE. That is genuine compounding—provided management deploys that ₹933 crore cash pile into high-return TPU and automated SCF lines rather than letting it sit idle or overpaying for acquisitions.

Before we leave the financial statements, let us check one final earnings-quality test: the relationship between Other Income and Operating Profit. In FY26, Garware reported ₹65 crore of Other Income on ₹774 crore of cash and liquid investments—roughly an 8.4% pre-tax treasury yield—and in TTM through September 2026, Other Income reached ₹77 crore on ₹933 crore of cash.

That tells us two things. First, the cash on the balance sheet is real and earning market-rate returns, not trapped in illiquid promoter-group loans. Second, when we value the core manufacturing business in Chapter 7, we must strip out that ₹77 crore of treasury income from operating EBITDA and value the ₹933 crore cash pile separately at 1x book—never capitalizing treasury interest at a 30x manufacturing multiple.

Finally, consider working capital discipline as scale increases. Despite holding higher strategic buffer inventory in the United States, Garware kept net working capital at just 29 days as of September 30, 2026—virtually unchanged from 28 days in FY26—because trade receivables sit at an extraordinary 7 to 9 days. Customers pay quickly, and supplier credit offsets much of the overseas stock.

Clean cash conversion is the ultimate lie detector in Indian mid-cap equities. When a company generates ₹1,817 crore of operating cash flow against ₹1,554 crore of cumulative net profit over ten years—while holding ₹933 crore of cash and zero long-term debt—you can trust that the reported margins reflect genuine economic earnings rather than aggressive accounting.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Ten consecutive years of positive Free Cash Flow, zero equity dilution, ₹933 crore in liquid reserves, and 7–9 debtor days establish GHFL as a genuine balance-sheet fortress. The headline 13.5% ROE understates core operating returns (>28% ex-cash), making future capital deployment of the ₹933 crore cash pile—and normalizing the 149 inventory days—the decisive financial storylines ahead.
